prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1028; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision in a parking area; the driver reports neck discomfort and a visit to urgent care the same day.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss; no coverage questions identified at this stage.

Entry 3: Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office. Requested the initial medical records and the police report.

Entry 4: Police report received and reviewed; it describes the same sequence of events the claimant gave at intake, and the other driver's statement agrees on the sequence and location.

Entry 5: Photographs from the scene and the vehicle inspection show front-end damage consistent with the impact described, and the estimate lines up with the reported force of the collision.

Entry 6: Spoke with two independent witnesses who each confirmed the collision happened as described; neither had any stake in the outcome.

Entry 7: Reviewed the vehicle history and prior claims; no earlier damage to this vehicle or the same front-end area is on record.

Entry 8: Medical records show a neck strain diagnosis, with a treatment plan of physical therapy and medication that followed a usual course; the claimant's reported improvement has been steady.

Entry 9: The claimant's account has stayed consistent across the recorded call, the written statement, and the follow-up interview through counsel; there is no record of earlier neck complaints. Seating position in the vehicle at impact is still not fully clear from the statements and will be clarified with counsel.

Entry 10: Treatment has tapered to periodic check-ins as recovery progresses; the file is being prepared for evaluation of the bodily injury claim with the medical records and repair documentation attached.
